gaps.sentence: He ___ be at work — I've just seen him at the beach.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' expresses something the evidence rules out.

gaps.sentence: The invoices ___ last week, so the delay is entirely our fault.
gaps.explanation: 'Should have + participle' criticises a past omission; passive adds 'been sent'.

gaps.sentence: You ___ to see that exhibition before it closes — it is outstanding.
gaps.hint: a strong recommendation with ought to
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' recommends something strongly: ought to see.

gaps.sentence: Visitors ___ to leave the gallery by 6 p.m.
gaps.hint: have to takes the full infinitive
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' takes the full infinitive with 'to': have to leave.

gaps.sentence: You ___ as well tell him the truth — he will find out anyway.
gaps.explanation: 'Might as well' suggests doing something because there is no reason not to: might as well.

gaps.sentence: Where is Anna? I am not sure — she ___ be in the library.
gaps.hint: an uncertain possibility, not really sure
gaps.explanation: 'Might' expresses a possibility the speaker is unsure about: might be.

gaps.sentence: Library books ___ be taken out of the reading room.
gaps.hint: a passive prohibition with mustn't be
gaps.explanation: Prohibitions can be passive: mustn't be taken.

gaps.sentence: In this lab, food and drink ___ be brought past the reception area.
gaps.explanation: Written prohibitions use 'must not': must not be brought.
